# Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **LEGO** | A unit of architecture with one owner, one reason to change, a public contract and a private implementation. Not every function is a LEGO. |
| **Domain LEGO** | A top-level LEGO representing a bounded area of the system. |
| **Feature LEGO** | A LEGO nested inside a domain, composed by its parent. |
| **Sub-LEGO** | A LEGO nested inside a feature. Depth 3 is the cap unless the Manager approves an exception. |
| **Public contract** | The only surface another LEGO may use. Stable, versioned, locked. |
| **Private implementation** | Everything else. Replaceable at any time without a contract version change. |
| **Contract version** | A promise. Major = breaking, minor = additive, patch = behaviour-preserving. |
| **Contract lock** | The file recording each public contract's current version, so drift is mechanically detectable. |
| **Envelope** | The metadata carried alongside every operation: identity, correlation, deadline, cancellation, idempotency, actor. Zero cost on direct in-process calls. |
| **Transport neutrality** | The same logical contract works in-process, in a worker, over WASM or remotely. `execute(request)` must never become inherently `HTTP POST /execute`. |
| **Capability** | A declared ability. Feature capabilities describe what a LEGO offers; security capabilities (network, filesystem, subprocess, secrets, native, env) must be granted explicitly. |
| **Trust level** | How much the system believes in the code: core, verified, community, untrusted. Trust never implies a capability. |
| **Failure boundary** | How far a failure can travel: in-process-safe, sandboxed, worker-isolated. Untrusted code must never be able to kill the trusted core. |
| **Data owner** | The single LEGO that owns a dataset. Others read it through its contract, never through its persistence. |
| **State class** | persistent, runtime, cache, configuration or derived. Unclassified hidden global state is forbidden. |
| **Blast radius** | How many other LEGOs a change can reach. Drives test selection. |
| **Strangler boundary** | The controlled edge around the legacy aggregate. It may shrink, never grow. |
| **Quarantine** | The mandatory holding state for a failed or suspect node. Evidence before deletion. |
| **Replay** | Capture inputs, replay them against another implementation, compare outputs. The mechanism that would make a JS-to-Rust swap provable. |
| **Activation** | available -> loaded -> active -> idle -> unloaded -> disabled. Nothing is forced into RAM. |

## Communication modes

- **call** — Synchronous direct contract call. The DEFAULT for in-process communication. _Use when:_ everything, unless another mode is specifically justified
- **event** — Asynchronous notification that something occurred or state changed. _Use when:_ state changes other LEGOs may care about; never for request/response
- **stream** — Continuous, ordered flow of items with backpressure. _Use when:_ execution output, logs, chat/AI token streams, large result sets
- **batch** — Many logical operations carried in one call to amortise overhead. _Use when:_ high-frequency small operations, especially across a future worker boundary

### Rules

- CALL is the default. A LEGO must not use EVENT or STREAM to avoid declaring a dependency.
- No HTTP between local LEGO. HTTP appears only at a real process or trust boundary.
- No message bus introduced to make the architecture look scalable.
- A contract declares WHICH modes an operation supports; the transport is chosen by the host, not baked into the contract.
- STREAM operations must declare a backpressure policy.
- EVENT delivery is at-most-once in-process today; a consumer that needs durability must say so and is a P11 concern.
